summary: Comprehensive backend tests for Tennant TMS iterations 2, 3, 4 — all 64 tests passing. Iter 2: PDF rendering (BOL/CI/Packing/Weight/COO all render with %PDF magic header), admin RBAC (list users, seed-team, role-change, all 401/403/200 paths), SAP S/4HANA mock (config, sales orders with plant filter, purchase orders with only_imports filter, sync RBAC: auditor=403 / dispatcher=200 / admin=200, logs persistence). Iter 3: AI Assistant single budget-safe Claude call (persists user+assistant msgs, history sorted oldest-first, user-scoped isolation, delete works), Webex fully mocked (config/spaces=7/meetings=4/notify writes log/schedule creates meeting/auth-protected). Iter 4: Workbook auto-seeds all 13 default tabs with correct names, columns array, create/rename/delete/404 paths, nested key projection (origin.city, destination.city), xlsx single-tab export (PK header, Content-Disposition), full-workbook xlsx export (PK header, larger byte count). Also updated iter-1 freight-bill tests to use auditor_client and onboarding decision to use admin_client (intentional RBAC change in iter 2).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1962 lines — recommend splitting into routers/modules (auth, shipments, freight_bills, sap, ai, webex, workbook, admin, documents) for maintainability. >700 line guideline exceeded.
Workbook KIND_DEFINITIONS uses dict reuse (shipments_expedites = shipments_tl); mutation in one would leak. Consider deep-copy or frozen schema.
AI chat: if EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is missing the user message is still persisted before the 500 is raised (pre-flight check is after the insert). Move the key check above the insert.
/api/admin/users uses sort('created_at', 1) but some seeded users may lack created_at — relies on lexicographic fallback; safe but worth normalizing.
Workbook export-all.xlsx is unbounded (loops all tabs/rows) — add a max-rows guard for safety in production.
Webex/SAP mocks return non-deterministic data on each call (random.choice/randint inside generators) — consider seeding random for stable snapshots.
